newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal no-confidence vote gains support.
newsitem.headline: Nepal no-confidence vote gains support.

text.p: A communist-led campaign to topple Nepal's 15-month old centre-right coalition gained strength on Monday with a small leftist group's promise to support a no-confidence motion being debated by parliament.

The Nepal Workers and Peasants Party (NWPP) said its three deputies in the House of Representatives would vote against Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba's three-party coalition government when the vote is taken, either on Monday or Tuesday.

NWPP's support for the no-confidence motion, which was put forth on Saturday by the opposition communist United Marxist-Leninist (UML) party, increases the chance of the government losing a close vote, politicians said.
Deuba's three-party coalition commands 108 seats in the 205-member house, whose actual strength is 200.
Constituents of the coalition are divided over support to the government.
Politicians estimate that the decision by NWPP will raise the number of votes in support of the motion to 104, just above the 103 votes required to pass it.
Deuba's Nepali Congress is demanding the disqualification of two defecting members of Nepal Sadbhavana Party (NSP), which could cost the opposition two crucial votes.
India's Asian Age newspaper said the Nepali Congress had flown five coalition deputies to Bangkok, fearing their defection. There was no independent confirmation of the report.
